title: convertd
description: convertd load per request, per stage and per pool, from the /metrics families in src/observability/metrics.rs.

list.name: scrape_interval
list.label: Scrape interval
list.description: The scrape interval of convertd, as a Prometheus duration such as 15s or 5m. Every query uses it as its min step, so $__rate_interval covers at least four scrapes.

panels.title: Requests / s
panels.description: POST /v1/convert outcomes that the handler records. A 401 from the auth layer and a failure to create the job directory are not counted.

panels.title: Error share
panels.description: Share of requests with a code other than OK.

targets.expr: (sum(rate(convert_requests_total{namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod", family=~"$family", code!="OK"}[$__rate_interval])) or vector(0)) / sum(rate(convert_requests_total{namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod", family=~"$family"}[$__rate_interval]))

panels.title: 429 share (all families)
panels.description: Share of requests refused with 429 TOO_MANY_REQUESTS: the queue, the queue wait or MAX_CONCURRENT_REQUESTS. It ignores the family filter, because a refusal before detection has family "unknown".

panels.title: Conversions in flight (estimate)
panels.description: The rate of the summed receive and total stage times (Little's law): from the start of the handler to the response head. The download of the body is not counted, and neither is an upload that fails (it records no stage). Each request adds its time when it finishes, so under steady load this is the mean number of conversions in progress. A conversion longer than the rate window counts in the window where it ends.

panels.title: Busy workers (mean)
panels.description: Mean of the busy worker count of all selected pods and pools together, over the rate window, sampled every $scrape_interval. A worker is busy from its lease to its return.

panels.title: Disk budget used
panels.description: Highest share of TMP_MAX_BYTES in use on one pod, at the end of the time range.

panels.title: Requests by HTTP status
panels.description: Outcomes of POST /v1/convert. convert_requests_total has a code label, not a status label: each series maps codes to the status from src/rest/response.rs. A 401 from the auth layer, a 404 for an unknown route and a failure to create the job directory are not counted. "other" catches a code that this map does not know.

panels.title: Errors by code
panels.description: Every request with a code other than OK, by error code.

panels.title: Errors since the process started
panels.description: The counter itself, per pod and code. A series starts at its first request with the value it has at the first scrape, so a rate does not show a first burst that ends between two scrapes; this panel does.

targets.expr: sum by (namespace, pod, code) (convert_requests_total{namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod", family=~"$family", code!="OK"})

panels.title: Successful requests by output and family
panels.description: 200 responses by requested output and detected input family.

targets.expr: sum by (output, family) (rate(convert_requests_total{namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod", family=~"$family", code="OK"}[$__rate_interval]))

panels.title: Responses cut after the head, since the process started
panels.description: 200 responses that convertd cut: RESPONSE_STALLED, RESPONSE_TOO_SLOW and RESPONSE_ABORTED. convert_requests_total counted them as OK at the head. A client that closes the connection itself is not counted. The counter starts again when the convertd process restarts. The counter itself, per pod: its series starts at the first cut with the value 1, so a rate would not show an isolated cut.

panels.title: p50 per stage
panels.description: Median duration of each stage of a request (Server-Timing stages). Short rate windows keep bursts visible.

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.5, sum by (le, stage) (rate(convert_stage_duration_seconds_bucket{namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod", stage=~"receive|detect|queue|preflight|convert|inspect|render|respond|engine|total", family=~"$family"}[$__rate_interval])))

panels.title: p99 per stage
panels.description: 99th percentile of each stage. A histogram quantile is an estimate inside its bucket.

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le, stage) (rate(convert_stage_duration_seconds_bucket{namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod", stage=~"receive|detect|queue|preflight|convert|inspect|render|respond|engine|total", family=~"$family"}[$__rate_interval])))

panels.title: Time in each stage (seconds per second)
panels.description: Rate of the summed time per stage, counted when each request finishes. Under steady load it estimates the requests in that stage at once. The stages overlap (an office preflight is inside convert, and receive is outside total), so the series do not add up and the panel does not stack them.

panels.title: Total and overhead by family, p50 and p99
panels.description: The total stage (from the end of the upload to the response head; the upload and the body download are outside it) and the overhead (total minus queue minus engine time) for each input family.

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.5, sum by (le, family) (rate(convert_stage_duration_seconds_bucket{namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod", stage="total", family=~"$family"}[$__rate_interval])))
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le, family) (rate(convert_stage_duration_seconds_bucket{namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod", stage="total", family=~"$family"}[$__rate_interval])))
histogram_quantile(0.5, sum by (le, family) (rate(convert_stage_duration_seconds_bucket{namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod", stage="overhead", family=~"$family"}[$__rate_interval])))
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le, family) (rate(convert_stage_duration_seconds_bucket{namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod", stage="overhead", family=~"$family"}[$__rate_interval])))

panels.title: Engine overhead per pool and op, p50 and p99
panels.description: Wall time of an engine call minus its queue and engine time: IPC, spawn and lease costs, per pool and operation.

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.5, sum by (le, pool, op) (rate(convert_engine_overhead_seconds_bucket{namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"}[$__rate_interval])))
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le, pool, op) (rate(convert_engine_overhead_seconds_bucket{namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"}[$__rate_interval])))

panels.title: Input size, p50 and p99
panels.description: Upload size per input family.

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.5, sum by (le, family) (rate(convert_input_bytes_bucket{namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod", family=~"$family"}[$__rate_interval])))
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le, family) (rate(convert_input_bytes_bucket{namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod", family=~"$family"}[$__rate_interval])))

panels.title: Queue depth per pool (max over the trailing rate window)
panels.description: Leases that wait for a worker. Each point is the maximum of the scraped samples in the trailing $__rate_interval (at least four scrapes), so a short queue stays visible when you zoom out, and one high sample shows in several points. A pool that never waited shows 0. The depth also counts the later engine calls of admitted requests. Only first calls count against QUEUE_CAPACITY (office: 2 x OFFICE_WORKERS) or 2 x RENDER_WORKERS, past which a request gets 429.

targets.expr: max by (namespace, pod, pool) (max_over_time(convert_queue_depth{namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"}[$__rate_interval])) or 0 * max by (namespace, pod, pool) (convert_workers{namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"})

panels.title: Workers per pool and state
panels.description: Workers that are idle, busy or starting, summed over the selected pods.

panels.title: Busy workers per pool and pod (max over the trailing rate window)
panels.description: Each point is the highest busy count of a pod over its scraped samples in the trailing $__rate_interval, so one high sample shows in several points.

targets.expr: max by (namespace, pod, pool) (max_over_time(convert_workers{namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod", state="busy"}[$__rate_interval]))

panels.title: Worker restarts by reason
panels.description: Workers that left the pool, by pool and reason: jobs, rss, age, timeout, crash, cancelled, error, start_failed. No series exists until the first restart.

panels.title: Worker restarts since the process started
panels.description: The counter itself. Its series starts at the first restart with the value 1, so increase() shows no isolated first restart; this panel does.

targets.expr: sum by (namespace, pod, pool, reason) (convert_worker_restarts_total{namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"$pod"})

panels.title: Supervisor RSS and peak
panels.description: Resident memory of the convertd serve process (VmRSS and VmHWM). Linux only.

panels.title: Supervisor threads and open descriptors
panels.description: Threads and open file descriptors of the supervisor. Linux only.

panels.title: Disk budget used versus the limit
panels.description: Bytes reserved under TMP_DIR against TMP_MAX_BYTES. A failed reservation gives 503.

panels.title: Warnings by code
panels.description: Manifest warnings per second, such as FONT_SUBSTITUTED or RENDER_CLAMPED.

panels.title: Warnings since the process started
panels.description: The counter itself, per pod. A code's series starts at its first warning with the value 1, so a rate does not show an isolated warning; this panel does.

panels.title: Skipped checks by check and reason
panels.description: Verification checks that did not run. blank_page counts pages.

panels.title: Pages rendered by format
panels.description: Image pages rendered per second.

options.content:
CPU time per worker call (user plus system), by pool and operation, arrives with effort O2 of ledger item 010. Its panels go in this row.

Until then, the stage durations above are wall time: a burst that uses six cores shows as time, not as cores.
